title: Chaining Events: eközben, a következő, egymás után

sections.title: Beyond *aztán*
sections.content: You already chain past events with *aztán*, *utána*, *később* and *előbb*. Three more tools let you describe HOW events relate to each other, not just that one came after another: *eközben* ("meanwhile") for something happening at the same time as something else, *a következő* + noun ("the next...") for naming the next specific thing in a sequence, and *egymás után* ("one after another") for a quick run of several events.

items.spanish: Én főztem, eközben Károly megterítette az asztalt.
items.english: I was cooking, meanwhile Károly set the table.

items.spanish: A következő nap korán felkeltünk, és tovább mentünk.
items.english: The next day we got up early and moved on.

items.spanish: Három telefon is jött egymás után, mindegyik rossz hírrel.
items.english: Three phone calls came one after another, each with bad news.

sections.content: *eközben* needs two things actually happening at once, so it pairs naturally with the *amikor*-style background sentences from Lesson 1 — *Amikor Károly dolgozott, eközben én bevásároltam* works well; using it for two things that clearly happened one after the other reads as a mistake.
